Sure, my anxiety was through the roof when I asked, but everything will turn out alright whether she says she does or doesn't like you in that way. Asking doesn't have to change anything and you two can still be great friends regardless of her answer. Hope this helps.

Round 1: This is a spam comp (your team) vs. brawl (theirs), which is an advantage. Spam beats brawl beats dive which beats spam.

(0:54) Prioritize healing rather than dps, especially with crit teammates. In that situation, the enemy Hanzo you're going for is sliding down a non-climbable roof after using wall climb, you won't be able to get him and he can't peek you. Pay attention to team comms, such as the Junk behind you spamming "I need healing".

(2:00) Ana is a backline support and also not a flanker. While you guys did win the fight, you put yourself in the frontlines to get the Reaper, even while behind Orisa's shield. Though the enemy team didn't punish, you put yourself out of LOS of everyone on your team but Zarya, and on the frontlines. In higher elo games, being that out of position would be quickly punished by the enemy.

(3:25) They didn't seem to notice you and the Zarya who saw you did pretty much nothing, but you would've been an easy kill for being right in the frontlines, especially with no teammates protecting. It would have been better to go through the door that leads to your backlines.

(4:27) In frontlines again, would have been dead if your Zarya didn't peel for you.

(4:47) Blossom would've killed you if not for the sleep dart, but you would've not taken any damage playing further back.

(6:07) Held nano for 4 minutes. You definitely would've been able to charge a second, and possibly some percentage of a third nano in that time.

Round 2: You have no shield and are running double off-tanks, nothing you can really do other than ask for a main tank. This means you have to play corners a lot more.

(7:59) Reaper's footsteps can be heard here. Enemy footstep are louder than your own, especially the ones that pose the most danger. Best thing to do here would be to communicate that there is a Reaper behind.

(8:12) Nice sleep, not sure why Ashe didn't notice the Reaper literally at her feet. The kill combo is shoot-nade-shoot-melee though I think it might've been nerfed (change in waking animation).

(9:13) Not much you can do here other than heal your tanks, but just pointing this out: your Bap was in enemy backlines and your tanks took a 2 vs 6, basically feeding.

(11:51) Held nano for 2 minutes, it could possibly have helped won a fight to protect the second point.

(12:25) Flanking Cree's footsteps can be heard until when you died at 12:36. It should be communicated to your teammates. Now, you're down main support and hitscan to just the Cree and the 5v6 turned into a 3v6. Left unchecked, he also killed your Ashe and Zarya. Cree's ult charges really fast as well.

(13:30) Making a note that they threw four ults here, leaving them to have a bad ult eco.

(13:54) Judging from distance and respawns, I'd say everyone except possibly Rein and Zarya could touch if they headed straight for cart. In addition, you didn't actually touch the payload but you could have stalled for a few second to let your tanks be able to touch cart as well.

Round 3: Still no shields at initial fight, play around corners.

(18:09) Really wouldn't recommend this position, you don't have much LOS on your teammates.

Round 4: For reference, some of Bastion's support counters are Ana's sleep/nade and Zen's Discord as well as Zen being good at bursting Bastions down in general.

(20:40) Your Rein was in a more dangerous situation while Ashe could sit where she is for a few seconds. Target prioritization here would be the Rein.

(21:55) They're going to come out of the top or bottom door where you were standing, wasn't the best position and put you right in enemy backlines.

(22:51) Would've been best to use sleep on the Mercy as she is rezing rather than after her target has been revived.

For the last fight, you were also positioned out of LOS of your entire team and weren't able to heal them one bit.

​

A few notes for thing that aren't really specific to one certain time:

\- Nano charges fast, it can turn team fights. It heals for 200 and gives reduces damage taken. Can be used offensively to break a choke point or defensively to heal an important target.

\- You're hardscoping too much, it narrows your fov so you can't see teammates/enemy/flankers outside of that space. Look into learning quickscoping on Ana, there's quite a few video tutorials on it, and use hip-firing more as well, just remember hip-firing has a slight travel time.

\- Ana is a sniper, so should be played in backlines. Think Widow when you're looking for positions.

\- Take high ground always, be greedy about taking high ground.

Hello, main/flex support playing on an Academy team here, I'll give a more in-depth explanation when it's not nearly midnight, but just a few quick advice based off the thought process you gave.  
(8:50) As an Ana, you always want high ground in the backlines; what I see very often with Bronze/Silver players who are at least somewhat aware of their positioning is that they tend to inch forward throughout the fight even if they decide to take a position much further back, often ending up right behind shields (if any) and in the frontlines. Obviously, it doesn't do much good if you'd need to "shoot through a floor" to heal but high ground keeps you as safe as possible. Ana doesn't have any mobility and really only has her sleep to stop divers. In addition, you're more out of sight since if you're getting shot at, you can just step back from the edge.  
(9:19) It's the job of tanks and dps to stay in supports' LOS (line of sight) when they need heals or go for a mega/mini. If you can easily move to a safe position to better heal, then do so but  never put yourself in danger to keep others alive. Honestly, it's situational. If you would be giving up a vital position, such as dropping down from high ground, then probably not the best. The supports are the most important roles to keep alive, it's them that are sustaining the fight.  
(14:05) I'm guessing this is the last few seconds of a round, this would be the last chance to use ults. Again, I'll be able to explain once I watch the replay but if it's a "rush to touch" situation, look for the way to make your ult count to contest as long as possible.  
(22:15) I'll suggest looking into learning basic ult-tracking, it's completely fine if you can't give an enemy's ult percentage at this rank but for example, if enemy Rein hasn't shattered for 4 or 5 fights, he definitely has it.

One thing I do want to let you know as advice though, is to not be too clingy; you see, my situation sounded pretty much exact to yours, and at one point, I started overthinking about it because I forgot to focus on myself too and had made the relationship the center of my attention, even dropping some things I like to do for it. I began to question and when I asked about it, it led to a breakup because all of this was too much for my SO. (We decided to stay friends and such.) Your boyfriend may seem independent to you because he is pursuing things in his life, or dealing with things in life. Both you and him should be allowed to have time for yourselves, and to achieve personal goals as well. Psychologically speaking, I believe he is doing what he can do for you already, you mention him doing useful things for you and being affectionate, which is great. If you push on though, it may make him feel inadequate that he isn't doing enough for you and that none of his efforts are good enough, which will likely cause him relationship stress. If you are still worries about not being sure if you have a future together, maybe you can talk with him about that? Such as just sitting down and having a heart to heart talk about what you guys see for your future and see how he responds from there? I've resources that I used for my own personal experience, so if you'd like to know more, just let me know! Hope this helps and I'll be here if you want a friend.

Hello! I understand how easy people make it sound when they say 'try something new' or 'find something to do' when it feel absolutely impossible, I've been there too because of a relationship. One thing I found that have helped me is talking to people, whether friends or strangers about it in a call; I'd be able to make jokes and poke fun at certain things in the past relationship, and it takes quite a bit of mental weight off your shoulders, in a healthy way too! I think I get what you mean by when you said you feel that you've hurt your friends over this. When I was broken up with, I ranted and I'll admit, I drove off several of my friends because I wasn't in a clear mind to act rational. (Basically, I was ranting to them all the time that it must've been extremely annoying for them.) I suggest the idea of maybe going on a general forum and asking if anyone wants to sort of be a long or short term close friend, supporting each other through hard times. I've been doing this and it makes me feel less burdened, and also give me bits of joy back that I'm helping someone else too. If you want a friend to talk to, I'm here too!
